extraction.name: LAMBADA
extraction.description: LAMBADA is a collection of narrative passages sharing the characteristic that human subjects are able to guess their last word if they are exposed to the whole passage, but not if they only see the last sentence preceding the target word.
extraction.creator: Denis Papemo, Germán Kruszewski, Angeliki Lazaridou, Quan Ngoc Pham, Raffaella Bemardi, Sandro Pezzelle, Marco Baroni, Gemma Boleda, Raquel Femández
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The data was sourced from the Book Corpus, filtered using language models to remove easy passages, and then evaluated by human subjects through crowdsourcing to ensure the target word could only be guessed from the broad context.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Duplicate removal, filtering out potentially offensive material with a stop word list, and filtering out passages that are relatively easy for standard language models.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human subjects guessed the target word based on the whole passage in two consecutive steps. If both guessed correctly, up to 10 more subjects tried to guess the target word based on the target sentence only. If no subject could guess it from the sentence alone, the passage was added.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The criteria for passage inclusion were very strict, requiring two consecutive subjects to exactly match the missing word and ensuring no subject out of ten could provide it based on local context only.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Up to 12 subjects per item (2 for broad context, up to 10 for local context)
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Proper names account for a consistent portion of the LAMBADA data.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing the capabilities of computational models for text understanding by means of a word prediction task requiring broad discourse context.

name.evidence: We introduce LAMBADA, a dataset to evaluate the capabilities of computational models for text understanding by means of a word prediction task.

description.evidence: LAMBADA is a collection of narrative passages sharing the characteristic that human subjects are able to guess their last word if they are exposed to the whole passage, but not if they only see the last sentence preceding the target word.

We filtered out passages that are relatively easy for standard language models, since such cases are likely to be guessable based on local context alone.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: 1. one human subject guessed the target word based on the whole passage... 2. a second subject guessed the target word based on the whole passage... 3. more subjects tried to guess the target word based on the target sentence only, until the word was guessed or the number of unsuccessful guesses reached 10; if no subject was able to guess the target word, the passage was added to the LAMBADA dataset.

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: A random sample of the remaining passages were then evaluated by human subjects through the CrowdFlower crowdsourcing service

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: Note that the criteria for passage inclusion were very strict: We required two consecutive subjects to exactly match the missing word, and we made sure that no subject (out of ten) was able to provide it based on local context only, even when given 3 guesses.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: The latter baseline aims at exploiting the potential bias that proper names account for a consistent portion of the LAMBADA data (see Figure 2 above).

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We thus propose LAMBADA as a challenging test set, meant to encourage the development of new models capable of genuine understanding of broad context in natural language text.
